Even granting that Kf4 is blocked by the knight on f4, the real issue is that allowing the king to reach f6 opens a window for White to exploit the newly opened e-file with Rxe8+ interpositions or queen checks once the knight leaves e5. Running the sequence h6+ Kf6 Ng4 through those resources shows that Black must first spend an extra tempo securing the back rank and coordinating the rooks (Kg7 Rf2 f4) before the final f6# can be delivered safely.
